metadata.name: join
metadata.displayName: join - Join lines of two files on a field
metadata.description: Join lines of two sorted files based on a common field

installation.note: join is commonly available by default as part of GNU coreutils

overview.summary: The join command combines lines from two files based on a common join field (like a key). It behaves similarly to a relational database join, but it expects input files to be sorted on the join field by default.
when_to_use: Merge two text files based on a shared key (like user id)
Combine reports exported as key/value files
Perform quick data joins without a database

syntax.description: By default, join uses the first whitespace-separated field as the key and expects both files to be sorted by that key.

options.description: Use CHAR as the field separator (default is whitespace)
Join on FIELD of FILE1 (1-based field index)
options.use_case: When the key is not the first column

options.description: Join on FIELD of FILE2 (1-based field index)
options.use_case: When the key is not the first column

options.description: Also print unpairable lines from file FILENUM (1 or 2)
options.use_case: When you want a full outer join-like output

examples.title: Join two files by the first column
examples.description: Combine records that share the same first field (key) in both files
examples.use_case: Merge simple reports keyed by an id

examples.title: Join CSV files on the first column
examples.description: Join two comma-separated files on their first column
examples.use_case: Combine CSV exports without importing into a spreadsheet

common_pitfalls.description: join expects both files to be sorted on the join field; otherwise output can be incomplete or incorrect.
common_pitfalls.solution: Sort first (e.g., sort -k1,1 users.txt > users.sorted) or use appropriate sort keys for your join field.

related_commands.description: Sort files by the join key before running join
Merge files side-by-side by line position (not by key)
Can implement more flexible joins with scripting
